svg.text: Microsoft Outlook Outage, 12 Nov 2026 · A Resilient Azure Redesign
Reference architecture for the failure class in Microsoft's post-incident report (EX1550543 / MO1550821) · workload-partitioned · cell-based · admission-controlled · store-and-forward
REGION A · North America East · 3 availability zones · one of 6 regions
ACCESS TIER · three workload pools, separated by hard bulkheads (red dashes)
SERVICE TIER · stateless, deadlines and retry budgets on every hop
Partition key = mailbox ID · each tenant is shuffle-sharded onto 4 of 53 cells (C(53,4) = 292,825 combinations)
MAIL TRANSPORT · accept durably first, deliver later
Accept = zone-redundant body write (Blob) + pointer (Event Hubs Premium, 90-day max retention) · only then SMTP 250 OK
Delivery is idempotent on Message-ID · retries for 48 h before any non-delivery report · poison messages to a DLQ topic
If every client-access cell is down, mail keeps being accepted and queued, so delay, not loss
updates a year) + a floor of
Page on symptoms, and watch the leading indicators
• per cell: handshake rate · lock wait · CPU/memory saturation · connection backlog
• failover load per destination cell · redirect rate · admit-to-shed ratio
• new-image vs old-image health delta (the canary signal)
• spool age · reconnect rate · time-to-first-byte from three outside vantage points
If mail is the incident, mail cannot be the channel
• SMS and voice to admins and incident staff via a separate stack
• Status page in another region and subscription, on a second DNS provider
• First customer notice target: ≤ 10 min after broad impact
• Backup MX accepts mail while client access is down
landed on the servers serving Exchange
Failover spread load region to region
Latent defect shipped broadly across fleet,

Reference redesign, NOT Microsoft's actual architecture; scale figures are illustrative assumptions · Independent analysis of Microsoft's public post-incident report; not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft · Azure is a trademark of Microsoft · Glyphs are simplified originals, not the official Azure icons
